retained_original_metadata.title: The Heisenberg-group two-body Hamiltonian with nonzero coupling and positive masses is not rationally Liouville-integrable on its algebraic phase cover
retained_original_metadata.author: Tomasz Stachowiak; Andrzej J. Maciejewski
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Non-Integrability of the Kepler and the Two-Body Problems on the Heisenberg Group
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof chooses a nonconstant complex trajectory and explicitly reduces its four-dimensional normal variational subsystem by a time-dependent triangularizing matrix. An exponential gauge then produces a parabolic-cylinder equation with non-solvable differential Galois identity component, yielding the integrability obstruction. The algebraic potential requires the supplied Poisson phase-space extension and the precise rational-integral limitation at irregular infinity.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Read the full Theorem3.1 proof, the two-body Hamiltonian and complex trajectory/variational matrices in Section3, and AppendixA explicit algebraic-cover Poisson extension. Morales-Ramis and Rehm parabolic-cylinder classification are established prior results; the new normal-system reduction and parameter calculation are explicit. AppendixA retains a routine correspondence lemma referred to the prior construction [8], with the Poisson matrix and lifted Hamiltonian supplied. The article explicitly limits irregular variational equations to rational integrals; preserve that narrower proof-supported scope despite the printed Theorem3.1 omitting the function-class qualifier. Exclude the mu=-1 branch whose exponential-solution obstruction is reported only as a Maple result.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem3.1 restricted to positive real nonzero masses m1,m2, nonzero real coupling kappa and rational first integrals in the phase coordinates and algebraic potential variable rho(g1^-1 g2), on the nonsingular cover defined in AppendixA. Thus mu=m1/m2>0 satisfies the printed mu!=-1 condition. No assertion of obstruction to arbitrary local meromorphic integrals or integrability on every individual energy level is added.
retained_original_metadata.editorial_warning: Scope notice: the author explicitly states on physical page2 that the non-Fuchsian variational equation supports only rational first integrals, and repeats the limitation in Section4. The printed Theorem3.1 has no function-class qualifier; this packet selects the stated rational scope, preserving the original theorem/proof bytes.
